entry.title: Tim Montana: The Five Riffs That Changed My Life

media:group.media:title: Tim Montana: The Five Riffs That Changed My Life
media:group.media:description:
Rock-country powerhouse @OfficialTimMontana sits down with Guitar World to reveal the exact guitar riffs that completely altered the course of his life. From getting personal, face-to-face lessons from ZZ Top’s Billy Gibbons, to the exact John Mayer and Blink-182 riffs he used as a "secret weapon" in Butte, Montana back in 2002, Tim doesn't hold anything back. He also shares the terrifying story of what it's really like to look across the stage and see Alice in Chains' Jerry Cantrell staring into your soul while you try to sing "Rooster," and why elitist guitar snobs are wrong about Kurt Cobain. Stick around until the end for the story about bootleg Nirvana merch and partying with Dave Grohl!

entry.title: Steve Morse on Van Halen, Lynyrd Skynyrd and why Fender didn't work

media:group.media:title: Steve Morse on Van Halen, Lynyrd Skynyrd and why Fender didn't work
media:group.media:description:
Guitar World's Matt sits down with Steve Morse at NAMM, to talk about the signature Music Man he's been refining for 40 years. Steve gets into why Fender and Guild never worked out, how pickup placement shapes his two-pickup blend, and why he treats the volume knob as his main effect rather than something you set and forget. He also talks about the new album Triangulation with Eric Johnson and John Petrucci, writing with his son, the homemade mute he built to work around his arthritis, and the six months he spent as an airline pilot before a gig he refused to cancel ended that career. Plus getting pulled on stage with Lynyrd Skynyrd, and what he learned watching Eddie Van Halen and Steve Lukather play behind a singer.

entry.title: We Played Jack White's Guitar Rig | Triplecaster, Klon and a brand-new pedal

media:group.media:title: We Played Jack White's Guitar Rig | Triplecaster, Klon and a brand-new pedal
media:group.media:description:
Guitar World's Mike Astley-Brown joins Jack White's guitar tech Dan Mancini, @OfficialTMR, for a walk through Jack's current tour rig, covering both pedalboards, the Pano Verb amp setup, and the guitars in the vault. And he even gets to play it.
Dan breaks down how the board is built for a show with no setlist, from the MXR Double Down he calls a secret weapon to the always-on Klon, the new Big Muff 2 and a first look at the Rototron. He also explains how the Pano Verbs recreate Jack's old two-amp White Stripes sound in one head, the B-benders added to his Triplecaster and Triplesonic, and the battered slide guitar that's been with Jack for over 20 years.
Read Mike's op-ed about the experience: https://www.guitarworld.com/artists/guitarists/i-played-jack-whites-guitar-rig

entry.title: Ben Kenney (Incubus, The Roots) on losing his hearing, leaving Incubus and his new rig

media:group.media:title: Ben Kenney (Incubus, The Roots) on losing his hearing, leaving Incubus and his new rig
media:group.media:description:
Ben Kenney played guitar and bass with The Roots, then spent 20 years as Incubus' bassist. While on tour, he found out he had a brain tumour that would permanently take the hearing in his right ear.
He sits down with Guitar World to talk about joining The Roots through Questlove, backing Jay-Z on MTV Unplugged, the surgeries that led him to step away from Incubus, and his current rig: a chambered Strandberg with Seymour Duncan Mark Holcomb pickups and a Quad Cortex profile of his Mesa Mini Rectoverb 25, run in stereo even though he can only hear in mono.
Follow Ben on socials: https://www.instagram.com/vatoben/
